p.title: Pink Ducks: partner-led growth strategy
p.sub: How an electric bike tour operator in Barcelona can sell direct, without depending on booking platforms
p.m1.v: Master's thesis, EAE Business School / Universitat de Lleida
p.m3.v: A team of three: Bulbuli Bala, Gracia Muhune Nyota and myself
p.b2: Pink Ducks sold almost everything through online travel agencies: high commissions, terms set by others, no direct link with the customer. The goal: a direct B2B channel, with no marketing budget.
p.b4: We wrote our assumptions down before going into the field, then tested them: six real interviews and nine market sources. A weighted criteria grid ranked the partners, and we stuck to it.
img.pink-segmentation: Partner segmentation built on trust: four tiers, from niche agencies to volume hotels. Source: Pink Ducks thesis report, Figure 3.
alt.pink-segmentation: Partner segmentation built on trust: four tiers, from niche agencies to volume hotels.
p.b6: Concierges at five-star hotels are not allowed to accept a commission or to display a QR code on their desk.
p.b7: Our whole incentive model rested on commission and QR-code tracking. On the most profitable segment it was unusable. We rebuilt it instead of ignoring it: for luxury hotels, a trust-based relationship with no commission, where the concierge books directly; QR-code tracking stayed only for hostels and four-star hotels.
img.pink-incentives: Three incentive models under one cost ceiling: net rate, relationship, volume commission. Source: Pink Ducks thesis report, Figure 4.
alt.pink-incentives: Three incentive models under one cost ceiling: net rate, relationship, volume commission.
p.b9.1.v: Ranked with weighted criteria, where outreach had none.
p.b9.2.v: Confidential net rates for agencies, a zero-commission relationship for luxury, tiered commissions for volume.
p.b9.3.v: With success and stop thresholds set in advance: fewer than 20% of contacted partners referring a booking within 60 days means stop.
p.b9.4.v: Rate cards, co-branded sheets, an operating protocol, and a system that makes every booking traceable.
p.b11: The strategy projects between €38,500 and €75,700 of additional net revenue in year one. We also wrote down plainly that trust-based relationships do not export: they have to be rebuilt city by city.
p.b12: What I take from it for running operations: a plausible assumption can be wrong, and only the field tells you. Setting thresholds before launch and rebuilding the model instead of working around it is factory discipline applied to a partnership.
p.b13: → The voice app built to absorb the volume: Barcelona CycleGuide

p.meta.desc: Master's thesis, 77 pages, written in a team of three: a direct B2B distribution channel for an electric bike tour operator. Six field interviews invalidated our main hypothesis and forced us to rebuild the model.
cm.title: Composting: recovering value from a coffee roaster's waste
cm.sub: How a waste stream nobody had measured became a 30,000 FCFA margin per tonne
cm.m1.v: Internship report, Saint-Jérôme Polytechnique (SJP3, process engineering)
cm.m2.v: Brûlerie Moderne, coffee roasting plant, Cameroon
cm.m4.v: Academic tutor Mme Kobbe Nathalie, company tutor Mr Passou Simplice
cm.b2: A coffee roasting plant produces chaff, separated from the beans during roasting, and wood shavings. The company threw both away, without even knowing the volume.
cm.b3: I quantified this unrecovered stream at 2,794 kg per year, a figure nobody at the company had ever calculated.
cm.b5: A real composting test at the Institute's microbiology lab: six containers, three of coffee chaff (R1 to R3) and three of wood waste (R4 to R6), followed for thirteen days with daily temperature readings, then a pH test. Results compared against a reference compost made in Côte d'Ivoire.
img.compost-temperature: Daily temperature of the coffee chaff containers (R1 to R3) during composting. Source: SJP3 internship report, Brûlerie Moderne, Figure 10.
alt.compost-temperature: Daily temperature of the coffee chaff containers (R1 to R3) during composting.
cm.b7: A lab test convinces nobody unless it ends with a number management understands. I compared the value of compost with poultry droppings, a competing fertiliser already sold in Cameroon, using prices observed in Yaoundé and Bafoussam.
img.compost-gains: Gain per tonne of compost compared with poultry droppings, in Bafoussam and Yaoundé: 30,000 FCFA in total. Source: SJP3 internship report, Brûlerie Moderne, Table 13.
alt.compost-gains: Gain per tonne of compost compared with poultry droppings, in Bafoussam and Yaoundé: 30,000 FCFA in total.
cm.b8: Result: a small-scale process proposed to the company would generate 30,000 FCFA of margin per tonne of fertiliser sold.
cm.b9: What I take from it for running operations
cm.b10: Measure what nobody measures, prove it with a trial, then translate it into value for the business: this was my first piece of work where a technical solution went all the way to a costed decision. A diagnosis that stays theoretical changes nothing.
cm.b11: → My engineering path, project by project

py.title: Pyrolysis: turning wood waste into biochar
py.sub: Run as a real project: objectives, milestones, a schedule, a 98,000 FCFA budget, and a hand-built reactor
py.m1.v: Supervised project, Saint-Jérôme Polytechnique (SJP4, process engineering)
py.b2: Treated and untreated wood waste accounts for around 27% of Cameroon's hazardous waste stream, close to 200,000 m³ sent to landfill every year. Can it become biochar instead of being buried?
py.b4: We ran it as a project, not as an improvised experiment: objectives, milestones, a schedule from March to July and a 98,000 FCFA budget, all set from the start.
img.pyro-planning: Project plan: tasks, dependencies and weekly schedule from March to July. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, Figure 2 and Table 1.
alt.pyro-planning: Project plan: tasks, dependencies and weekly schedule from March to July.
img.pyro-budget: Project budget: rig, metal plate, sensors, transport, contingency, 98,000 FCFA in total. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, Table 2.
alt.pyro-budget: Project budget: rig, metal plate, sensors, transport, contingency, 98,000 FCFA in total.
py.b6: A lab-scale fixed-bed reactor fed with vène wood chips, instrumented by ourselves: a mass sensor and a PT100 temperature sensor wired to an Arduino board, with the wiring simulated first in Proteus 8 to check the circuit before building it.
img.pyro-bois: Some of the wood types studied. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, Figure 4.
alt.pyro-bois: Some of the wood types studied.
img.pyro-dechets: The wood waste used in the trial. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, Figure 18.
alt.pyro-dechets: The wood waste used in the trial.
img.pyro-reacteur: Isometric view of the reactor geometry, split into two parts: the furnace and the feed chamber. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, reactor geometry.
alt.pyro-reacteur: Isometric view of the reactor geometry, split into two parts: the furnace and the feed chamber.
py.b8: Mass and temperature were logged every five to fifteen minutes, from room temperature to over 550°C: a heating rate of 33.6 K per minute. We calculated the activation energy with two reference methods so they could check each other: Kissinger-Akahira-Sunose 0.81 kJ/mol and Miura-Maki 1.31 kJ/mol. The regression gives a coefficient of determination of R² = 0.975.
img.pyro-temperature: Temperature recorded over time during the thermal treatment. Source: SJP4 supervised project report, page 37.
alt.pyro-temperature: Temperature recorded over time during the thermal treatment.
py.b10: A two-part reactor, a furnace and a feed chamber, with a condensation flask to capture condensable gases. Treating the harmful gases is part of the project: we did not leave it out of scope.
py.b11: What I take from it for running operations: you cannot measure a phenomenon without an instrument, so you build the instrument, and you hold it all together with objectives, milestones and a budget.
py.b12: → My engineering path, project by project

k.title: Kribi: reducing oily-water discharge from a gas power plant
k.sub: How 200 of 250 maintenance interventions led to a data-driven diagnosis, then a leak detection system
k.m1.v: Final-year engineering thesis, Saint-Jérôme Polytechnique (SJP5, process engineering)
k.m2.v: Kribi Power Development Company, a 216 MW gas-fired power plant, Cameroon
k.m4.v: Individual work. Supervisors: Mr. Etonde Eyidi Yannick (academic), Mr. Wouambo Marius (shift supervisor)
k.b2: The plant produces 216 MW from thirteen dual-fuel Wärtsilä 50DF engines. They generate oily water that must be treated before any discharge. Three signals were rising together and nobody had linked them: the volume of oily water removed, breakdowns of the treatment unit, and lubricating oil consumption.
k.b3: In 2021, 200 of the 250 maintenance interventions in the engine room were due to oil leaks: 80% of maintenance activity spent on a single type of failure.
k.b4.3.k: Breakdowns of the SENITEC treatment unit
k.b4.3.v: 1 in 2019, 3 in 2020, 7 in 2021, and already 7 in early 2022.
k.b6.1.v: Do the signals move together? A correlation of 0.92 between sludge and oil consumption, and 0.98 between sludge recovered and interventions on the treatment unit. The plant was paying three times for the same loss: in oil purchases, engine maintenance and treatment-unit maintenance.
k.b6.2.v: Where does the oil escape? 20% of the equipment accounts for 80% of leaks: rocker arm covers, pipelines, valves, inspection covers, pumps and camshafts. Monitoring thirteen entire engines is not feasible, monitoring six families of leak points is.
k.b6.3.v: Why was the treatment unit breaking down more and more? A cause diagram applied to the SENITEC unit.
img.k.1: Tracking engine parameter trends, 2019 to 2021, the data series behind the 0.92 correlation. Source: SJP5 engineering thesis, Kribi Power.
alt.k.1: Tracking engine parameter trends, 2019 to 2021, the data series behind the 0.92 correlation.
img.k.2: Ishikawa diagram on the SENITEC unit's failures, sorted into five families of causes. Source: SJP5 engineering thesis, Kribi Power.
alt.k.2: Ishikawa diagram on the SENITEC unit's failures, sorted into five families of causes.
k.b8: An ultraviolet oil leak detection and location system focused on the six equipment families from the Pareto analysis: catch a leak the moment it appears, and monitor only what actually breaks.
k.b9: What I take from it for running operations: measure before acting, check whether signals move together, target the minority responsible for most failures, then propose a proportionate solution. It is my method for any recurring problem, on a production line as in a team.
k.b10: → My engineering path, project by project

bc.title: Barcelona CycleGuide: a voice app that guides, warns, and tells the story
bc.sub: Designed, coded, tested and delivered with an AI development assistant, for an electric bike tour operator
bc.m1.v: Personal project, delivered to the founder of Pink Ducks
bc.m3.v: Solo work, paired with an AI development assistant
bc.m4.v: Functional prototype, tested on real iOS and Android devices
bc.b2: A bike guide can only accompany one group at a time, in one language, and only during the tour. Can some of that value remain once the guide is gone, without the cyclist stopping to look at a screen?
bc.b4: The guiding principle fits in one sentence: the cyclist should never have to stop, look down, or search. Everything triggers on its own or is controlled by voice.
bc.b5.1.v: An invisible circle of around 40 metres surrounds each place: as soon as the cyclist enters it, the story of the place is read aloud.
bc.b5.2.v: The app warns before the infringement, not after. Prevention, in the literal sense.
bc.b5.3.v: A conversational AI that answers spoken questions, aware of the cyclist's location.
bc.b5.4.v: Manoeuvres announced by voice, automatic rerouting, and the city's open Bicing and Bicibox data in real time.
bc.b6: Tech stack: React Native and Expo (SDK 54) for iOS and Android, Firebase, a custom-built geofencing engine (Haversine formula), a Claude integration, OSRM routing, EAS Build and GitHub Actions.
img.bc.1: The Gothic Quarter entry opens on its own at the edge of the zone, with the regulatory warning and the fine at stake.
alt.bc.1: The Gothic Quarter entry opens on its own at the edge of the zone, with the regulatory warning and the fine at stake.
img.bc.2: A recalculated route flags that it crosses two no-cycling zones before the cyclist enters them.
alt.bc.2: A recalculated route flags that it crosses two no-cycling zones before the cyclist enters them.
img.bc.3: The voice assistant answers safety questions based on the cyclist's actual location.
alt.bc.3: The voice assistant answers safety questions based on the cyclist's actual location.
img.bc.4: The assistant's home screen offers frequent questions in one tap: parking, safety, local rules.
alt.bc.4: The assistant's home screen offers frequent questions in one tap: parking, safety, local rules.
img.bc.5: Two preset guided routes, each with distance, duration and number of stops calculated in advance.
alt.bc.5: Two preset guided routes, each with distance, duration and number of stops calculated in advance.
img.bc.6: Parking search relies on the city's open data. Here, no free spot within 500 metres.
alt.bc.6: Parking search relies on the city's open data. Here, no free spot within 500 metres.
bc.b7: The three decisions that made the project
bc.b8.1.v: The first prototype ran on FlutterFlow. The limits of the free tier blocked the GPS and AI libraries, the core of the product. I stopped after a phase and a half instead of working around it.
bc.b8.2.v: A full switch to React Native and Expo: a free, extensible foundation that would no longer hit a ceiling.
bc.b8.3.v: The Radar.io service rejected sign-ups using a personal address. Rather than drop the feature that gives the app its point, I implemented proximity detection myself with the Haversine formula: three hours of work, and the dependency was gone.
bc.b10: On real iPhone and Android devices, via a development server. The voice pipeline was debugged with an on-screen diagnostic overlay that traced every step. Geofencing was tested inside and outside Barcelona, and every supported language was checked on screen and by voice.
bc.b11: This is a functional prototype still being tested, not a product in production. The handover document given to the founder lists the current limitations itself, without dressing them up. That is how I present a deliverable.
bc.b12: What I take from it for running operations
bc.b13: Facing a technical wall with nobody to help: I switch platforms when one hits its limit, I write the function myself when a service closes the door, and I finish with a document a non-technical founder can read. A deliverable nobody else can pick up is not a deliverable.

pa.title: Five years, five fieldwork projects, one common thread
pa.sub: Food process engineering degree, Saint-Jérôme Polytechnique de Douala, 15/20, with Distinction
pa.m4.v: A documented fieldwork project every year, from first to fifth year
pa.b1: I had not planned it: four of my five projects deal with the same question. What do you do with what a facility discharges: avoid it, or turn it into something useful? Each one also taught me to measure, prove, then put a number on it.
pa.b2: 2022 · Reducing oily water discharge from a gas power plant
pa.b3: SJP5 · Final-year thesis · Kribi Power Development Company
pa.b4: A 216 MW plant, thirteen engines, and 200 of 250 maintenance interventions caused by oil leaks. A 0.92 correlation between sludge and oil consumption, a Pareto showing 20% of equipment behind 80% of leaks, an Ishikawa of the treatment unit, and a UV detection system proposed.
pa.b5: → Read the full write-up of this thesis
pa.b6: 2021 · Recovering value from wood waste through pyrolysis
pa.b7: SJP4 · Supervised project · Paired with Vannick Baombé
pa.b8: Wood waste makes up around 27% of Cameroon's hazardous waste, close to 200,000 m³ in landfill. We studied slow pyrolysis and designed a two-part reactor, building in the treatment of harmful gases. Run as a project, with objectives, milestones, a schedule and a budget.
img.pa.1: Process flow diagram of the studied process, from waste pretreatment to gas and pyrolysis oil treatment.
alt.pa.1: Process flow diagram of the studied process, from waste pretreatment to gas and pyrolysis oil treatment.
pa.b9: → Read the full write-up of this project
pa.b10: 2020 · Composting waste from a coffee roasting plant
pa.b12: A roasting plant threw away its chaff and shavings without knowing the volume. I quantified the stream at 2,794 kg per year, ran a composting trial on six containers over thirteen days, then an economic case: 30,000 FCFA of margin per tonne of fertiliser sold. My first piece of work where a technical solution becomes value for the business.
pa.b13: → Read the full write-up of this report
pa.b14: 2019 · Sesame oil and a natural pesticide based on nkui spices
pa.b15: SJP2 · Practical coursework · February to April 2019
pa.b16: Producing sesame oil, and assisting on the manufacture of a natural pesticide based on nkui spices, including African pepper, known for its insecticidal properties. I say "assisting" on purpose: I took part, I did not lead.
pa.b17: 2018 · First immersion in a thermal power plant
pa.b18: SJP1 · Internship report · Dibamba Power Development Company
pa.b19: Operations department on a shift rotation: inspection rounds, handovers between shift teams, daily production reports, Saturday checks and safety verifications. That is where I received my first formal safety induction and saw an industrial safety culture from the inside, not from a classroom.
pa.b20: What this sequence says about me
pa.b21: Four years separate my first internship from my thesis, and both took place in a thermal power plant (Dibamba, then Kribi). From the field to a costed decision: it is the same question that links process engineering to a company's economics, and the one I carry into operations today.
